steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Rights and responsibilities are two sides of the same citizenship coin. Rights: what you are entitled to (vote, free speech, fair trial, education, healthcare). Responsibilities: what you owe to society (obey the law, pay taxes, vote, serve on a jury, respect others' rights).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Legal responsibilities: obey the law (criminal and civil law apply to all), pay taxes (income tax, VAT, council tax fund public services), and serve on a jury if called (criminal trials require 12 jurors to determine guilt). Jury service is a civic duty - you can be fined for not attending without good reason.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Civic responsibilities: vote in elections (not legally required but considered a civic duty), engage with political issues, volunteer in the community, and treat others with respect regardless of background. These are not legally enforced but are expected of good citizens.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The balance between rights and responsibilities: your right to free speech comes with the responsibility not to incite hatred; your right to protest comes with the responsibility to do so peacefully; your right to education comes with the responsibility to attend school until 18. Rights without responsibilities lead to selfish individualism; responsibilities without rights lead to oppression.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Explain the difference between a citizen's legal responsibilities and civic responsibilities, giving examples of each. | Q: Evaluate whether voting should be compulsory in the UK. | Q: Assess the importance of active citizenship for a healthy democracy.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Legal = enforced by law (obey law, pay tax, jury service). Civic = expected but not enforced (vote, volunteer, engage). Compulsory voting: FOR = representation, legitimacy. AGAINST = liberty, quality of votes. Active citizenship = practical action (campaigning, volunteering, participation). Democracy needs active citizens to function.
